name: Chicken noodle stir-fry
summary: Egg noodles stir-fried with chicken, red pepper, carrot and broccoli in a soy and oyster sauce.
method: Cook the dry egg noodles in boiling water for 4 minutes, drain, rinse under cold water and toss with the sesame oil.

Slice the chicken breast into thin strips. Slice the red pepper and carrot into matchsticks and cut the broccoli into small florets. Slice the spring onions and grate the garlic and ginger. Mix the soy sauce and oyster sauce with 2 tablespoons of water.

Heat the vegetable oil in a wok over a high heat and stir-fry the chicken for 4 to 5 minutes until cooked through. Add the garlic and ginger for 30 seconds, then the vegetables for 3 to 4 minutes until just tender.
Add the noodles and sauce and toss over the heat for 1 to 2 minutes until hot and glossy. Scatter over the spring onions.

name: Beef noodle stir-fry
summary: Egg noodles stir-fried with thin strips of sirloin and crisp vegetables in a soy and oyster sauce.
method: Cook the dry egg noodles in boiling water for 4 minutes, drain, rinse under cold water and toss with the sesame oil.

Trim the beef steak and slice it thinly across the grain. Slice the red pepper and carrot into matchsticks and cut the broccoli into small florets. Slice the spring onions and grate the garlic and ginger. Mix the soy sauce and oyster sauce with 2 tablespoons of water.

Heat half the vegetable oil in a wok over a very high heat and stir-fry the beef in two batches for 1 to 2 minutes until browned; lift out. Add the rest of the oil, the garlic and ginger for 30 seconds, then the vegetables for 3 to 4 minutes.
Return the beef, add the noodles and sauce and toss for 1 to 2 minutes until hot and glossy. Scatter over the spring onions.
notes: The chicken noodle stir-fry with lean sirloin in place of the chicken.

name: Prawn noodle stir-fry
summary: Egg noodles stir-fried with prawns and crisp vegetables in a soy and oyster sauce.
method: Cook the dry egg noodles in boiling water for 4 minutes, drain, rinse under cold water and toss with the sesame oil.

Pat the peeled prawns dry. Slice the red pepper and carrot into matchsticks and cut the broccoli into small florets. Slice the spring onions and grate the garlic and ginger. Mix the soy sauce and oyster sauce with 2 tablespoons of water.

Heat the vegetable oil in a wok over a high heat and stir-fry the prawns for 2 to 3 minutes until pink; lift out. Add the garlic and ginger for 30 seconds, then the vegetables for 3 to 4 minutes until just tender.
Return the prawns, add the noodles and sauce and toss for 1 to 2 minutes until hot and glossy. Scatter over the spring onions.
notes: Weigh the prawns peeled. The chicken noodle stir-fry with prawns in place of the chicken.

name: Tofu noodle stir-fry
summary: Egg noodles stir-fried with golden tofu and crisp vegetables in a soy and honey sauce.
method: Cook the dry egg noodles in boiling water for 4 minutes, drain, rinse under cold water and toss with the sesame oil.

Press the tofu between kitchen paper for 10 minutes and cut it into cubes. Slice the red pepper and carrot into matchsticks and cut the broccoli into small florets. Slice the spring onions and grate the garlic and ginger. Mix the soy sauce and honey with 2 tablespoons of water.

Heat the vegetable oil in a wok over a medium-high heat and fry the tofu for 6 to 8 minutes, turning, until golden; lift out. Add the garlic and ginger for 30 seconds, then the vegetables for 3 to 4 minutes until just tender.
Return the tofu, add the noodles and sauce and toss for 1 to 2 minutes until hot and glossy. Scatter over the spring onions.
notes: The chicken noodle stir-fry with tofu in place of the chicken, and honey in place of the oyster sauce so it stays meat-free.

name: Vegetable noodle stir-fry
summary: Egg noodles stir-fried with peppers, carrot, broccoli, mangetout and beansprouts in a soy and honey sauce.
method: Cook the dry egg noodles in boiling water for 4 minutes, drain, rinse under cold water and toss with the sesame oil.

Halve the mangetout. Slice the red pepper and carrot into matchsticks and cut the broccoli into small florets. Slice the spring onions and grate the garlic and ginger. Mix the soy sauce and honey with 2 tablespoons of water.
Heat the vegetable oil in a wok over a high heat, add the garlic and ginger for 30 seconds, then the red pepper, carrot, broccoli and mangetout for 3 to 4 minutes until just tender.
Add the noodles, beansprouts and sauce and toss for 1 to 2 minutes until hot and glossy. Scatter over the spring onions.
notes: The chicken noodle stir-fry with more vegetables in place of the chicken, and honey in place of the oyster sauce.

name: Egg noodle stir-fry
summary: Egg noodles stir-fried with soft scrambled egg and crisp vegetables in a soy and honey sauce.
method: Cook the dry egg noodles in boiling water for 4 minutes, drain, rinse under cold water and toss with the sesame oil.

Beat the eggs. Slice the red pepper and carrot into matchsticks and cut the broccoli into small florets. Slice the spring onions and grate the garlic and ginger. Mix the soy sauce and honey with 2 tablespoons of water.

Heat a third of the vegetable oil in a wok, pour in the eggs and stir until softly set; tip onto a plate. Add the rest of the oil, the garlic and ginger for 30 seconds, then the vegetables for 3 to 4 minutes until just tender.
Add the noodles and sauce and toss for 1 to 2 minutes, then fold the eggs back through and scatter over the spring onions.
notes: The chicken noodle stir-fry with scrambled eggs in place of the chicken, and honey in place of the oyster sauce.

name: Peanut noodles
summary: Egg noodles tossed in a creamy peanut, lime and soy sauce with crunchy raw vegetables and peanuts.
method: Whisk the peanut butter, soy sauce, lime juice, honey, sriracha, grated garlic and ginger with the hot water until smooth.
Cook the dry egg noodles in boiling water for 4 minutes, then drain.
Cut the carrot, red pepper and cucumber into thin matchsticks and slice the spring onions.
Toss the warm noodles with the sauce and vegetables, then top with the chopped peanuts and coriander. Eat warm or cold.

name: Sesame noodles
summary: Chilled soba noodles in a soy and toasted sesame dressing with edamame, cucumber and spring onions.
method: Toast the sesame seeds in a dry pan for 2 to 3 minutes until golden, then tip out.
Whisk the soy sauce, sesame oil, cider vinegar, honey and grated garlic and ginger together.
Cook the dry soba noodles in boiling water for 4 to 5 minutes, adding the edamame for the last 3 minutes. Drain and rinse under cold water until cool.
Toss the noodles and edamame with the dressing, sliced cucumber and spring onions, then scatter with the sesame seeds and the chilli flakes if you like. Serve cold.
notes: Rice vinegar is not in the catalogue, so cider vinegar is used.

name: Ginger chicken noodle soup
summary: Gingery chicken broth with poached shredded chicken, rice noodles and pak choi.
method: Put the chicken stock in a saucepan with the sliced ginger and garlic, the soy sauce and fish sauce, and bring to a gentle simmer.
Add the whole chicken breast and poach it gently for 12 to 15 minutes until cooked through. Lift it out and shred it with two forks.
Meanwhile, soak or boil the dry rice noodles as the packet says, then drain and divide between two bowls.
Add the pak choi to the simmering broth for 2 minutes, then return the chicken and add the lime juice.
Ladle the broth, chicken and pak choi over the noodles and top with the spring onions, red chilli and coriander.

name: Vegetable noodle soup
summary: Gingery vegetable broth with mushrooms, carrot, pak choi and rice noodles.
method: Put the vegetable stock in a saucepan with the sliced ginger and garlic and the soy sauce, and bring to a gentle simmer.
Add the sliced mushrooms and the carrot cut into thin matchsticks and simmer for 6 to 8 minutes until tender.
Meanwhile, soak or boil the dry rice noodles as the packet says, then drain and divide between two bowls.
Add the pak choi to the broth for 2 minutes, then stir in the lime juice.
Ladle the broth and vegetables over the noodles and top with the spring onions, red chilli and coriander.
notes: The ginger chicken noodle soup with mushrooms and carrot in place of the chicken, vegetable stock, and no fish sauce.

name: Rice noodle salad
summary: Cold rice vermicelli with crunchy vegetables, herbs and peanuts in a lime and fish sauce dressing.
method: Stir the fish sauce, lime juice, sugar, finely chopped garlic and red chilli with the water until the sugar dissolves.
Cover the dry rice vermicelli with boiling water for 3 to 5 minutes until soft, then drain, rinse under cold water and drain well.
Cut the carrot and cucumber into thin matchsticks, slice the spring onions and pick the mint and coriander leaves.
Toss the noodles with the vegetables, beansprouts, herbs and dressing, add the cooked prawns if using, and top with the chopped peanuts.

name: Teriyaki chicken bowl
summary: Chicken thighs in a sticky homemade teriyaki-style glaze over jasmine rice with steamed broccoli.
method: Rinse the dry rice and put it in a lidded saucepan with 210 ml water. Bring to the boil, cover and cook on a low heat for 12 minutes, then rest off the heat for 5 minutes.
For the sauce, mix the soy sauce, honey, cider vinegar, grated garlic and ginger, cornflour and the 60 ml water until smooth.

Heat the vegetable oil in a frying pan and cook the chicken thighs for 5 to 6 minutes on each side until cooked through. Pour in the sauce and let it bubble for 2 to 3 minutes, turning the chicken, until thick and glossy.
Steam the broccoli for 4 minutes. Slice the chicken and serve over the rice with the broccoli, spooning over the sauce and scattering with the spring onions and sesame seeds.
notes: The glaze uses honey and a little cider vinegar because mirin is not in the catalogue.

name: Sweet chilli tofu noodles
summary: Crisp cornflour-coated tofu and stir-fried vegetables tossed with rice noodles in a homemade sweet chilli sauce.
method: Press the tofu between kitchen paper for 10 minutes, cut it into cubes and toss in all but 1 teaspoon of the cornflour.

For the sweet chilli sauce, whisk the honey, cider vinegar, finely chopped red chilli and garlic, soy sauce, the water and the last teaspoon of cornflour in a small saucepan, then simmer, stirring, for 2 minutes until thickened.
Soak or boil the dry rice noodles as the packet says, then drain.
Heat the vegetable oil in a wok and fry the tofu for 6 to 8 minutes, turning, until crisp and golden; lift out. Stir-fry the sliced red pepper and mangetout for 3 minutes.
Return the tofu, add the noodles and sweet chilli sauce, toss for 1 minute and scatter with the spring onions.
notes: Bottled sweet chilli sauce is not in the catalogue, so a quick version is made from honey, vinegar and fresh chilli.

name: Instant noodles with egg and vegetables
summary: A packet of instant noodles made into a fuller bowl with a poached egg, spinach and mushrooms.
method: Bring the water to the boil in a small saucepan and add the sliced mushrooms for 1 minute.
Add the noodle block and cook for 2 minutes, then stir in the seasoning sachet.
Crack in the egg, add the spinach, cover and simmer for 2 to 3 minutes until the white is set and the spinach has wilted.
Tip into a bowl and scatter with the sliced spring onion.
notes: USDA has one record for instant noodles and their flavour sachet together, so both lines use it. Leaving out some or all of the sachet takes off its weight, but understates the salt removed, because the sachet carries most of the salt. If your pack has a separate oil sachet, add it as an oil line.

name: Ramen-style broth bowl
summary: Miso and chicken stock broth with egg noodles, jammy eggs, pak choi, mushrooms and sweetcorn.
method: Lower the eggs into boiling water and cook for 6 and a half minutes, then cool in cold water and peel.

Simmer the chicken stock with the grated garlic and ginger and the sliced mushrooms for 10 minutes. Take off the heat, whisk the miso with a ladle of the broth until smooth, then stir it back in with the soy sauce and sesame oil.
Cook the dry egg noodles in boiling water for 4 minutes, adding the pak choi for the last minute, then drain and divide between two bowls.
Ladle the broth and mushrooms over the noodles, add the pak choi, sweetcorn and halved eggs, and scatter with the spring onions and the chilli flakes if you like.
notes: Ramen-style rather than a traditional ramen: wheat egg noodles stand in for fresh ramen noodles. Do not boil the broth after adding the miso.

name: Coconut curry noodle soup
summary: Rice noodles in a curry-spiced coconut and chicken broth with sliced chicken, beansprouts and lime.
method: Heat the vegetable oil in a saucepan and soften the finely chopped onion for 5 minutes. Add the grated garlic and ginger, the sliced red chilli, curry powder and turmeric and stir for 1 minute.
Pour in the coconut milk and chicken stock, add the fish sauce and brown sugar and bring to a simmer.
Slice the chicken breast thinly, add it to the soup and simmer for 6 to 8 minutes until cooked through.
Meanwhile, soak or boil the dry rice noodles as the packet says, then drain and divide between two bowls.
Stir the lime juice into the soup, ladle it over the noodles and top with the beansprouts and coriander.
notes: Made with curry powder and fresh aromatics; jarred curry pastes are not in the catalogue.

name: Pad Thai-style noodles
summary: Stir-fried rice noodles with chicken, egg, beansprouts and spring onions in a sweet-sour lime and fish sauce, topped with peanuts.
method: Soak the dry rice noodles in warm water for 15 to 20 minutes until bendy but still firm, then drain.
Stir the fish sauce, lime juice, brown sugar and chilli flakes together until the sugar dissolves.

Heat the vegetable oil in a wok over a high heat and stir-fry the thinly sliced chicken breast for 4 minutes. Add the crushed garlic for 30 seconds, then push everything to one side, crack in the eggs and scramble until just set.
Add the noodles and sauce and toss for 2 to 3 minutes until the noodles are tender and have soaked up the sauce. Add the beansprouts and the spring onions cut into lengths and toss for 30 seconds.
Serve scattered with the chopped peanuts and the coriander if you like.
notes: Pad Thai-style rather than a traditional recipe. Tamarind is not in the catalogue, so lime juice and brown sugar give the sour-sweet balance.

name: Singapore-style noodles
summary: Thin rice vermicelli stir-fried with curry powder, prawns, egg ribbons, red pepper and beansprouts.
method: Soak the dry rice vermicelli in boiling water for 3 to 4 minutes until just soft, then drain and rinse under cold water.
Heat a little of the vegetable oil in a wok, add the beaten egg and swirl into a thin omelette. Roll it up, slice into ribbons and set aside.

Add the rest of the oil and stir-fry the prawns for 2 minutes until pink; lift out. Stir-fry the sliced onion and red pepper for 3 minutes, then add the garlic, ginger, curry powder and turmeric for 30 seconds.

Add the noodles, soy sauce and 2 tablespoons of water and toss until the noodles are evenly coloured and hot. Return the prawns and egg, add the beansprouts and spring onions and toss for 1 minute more. Finish with the sesame oil.
